title: Rabbi Naftali

paragraphs: At the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Taanit chapter 4, he was a priest with a crooked finger, and he asked Rabbi Mana II whether he could ascend the platform to give the priestly blessing. There is also Rav Yitzchak bar Naftali in Ketubot 96a.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Mana II preserves the source’s ב׳. The text records Naftali’s question, not its answer. The separate Yitzchak bar Naftali is not automatically identified as his son.

The checked Jerusalem Ta’anit passage has Naftali of the crooked finger asking Mana and then gives a conditional permission. Hyman’s notice preserves the question alone; no answer is inserted into it. The ordinal Mana II remains Hyman’s identification. The separate Yitzchak bar Naftali transmission does not establish that he was this Naftali’s son.
